articles.headline: Commanders' Quinn, Daniels discuss QB's throwaway on fourth-down play
articles.description: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels shouldn't have thrown a fourth-down pass away in the second quarter of Monday night's loss, coach Dan Quinn said.
articles.headlineJa: コマンダーズのクイン監督とダニエルズ、4ダウン目のスローアウェイについて語る
articles.descriptionJa: コマンダーズのダン・クイン監督は、月曜夜の敗戦における第2クォーター、QBジェイデン・ダニエルズが4ダウン目でパスをスローアウェイすべきではなかったと述べた。
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels shouldn't have thrown a fourth-down pass away in the second quarter of Monday night's 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, coach Dan Quinn said.

On a fourth-and-2 from the 49ers' 13-yard line, Daniels dropped back to pass and left the pocket after the 49ers started to generate pressure.

As Daniels ran to his right, two defenders pursued him, including linebacker Fred Warner. A flag was also thrown in front of Daniels. He could not make the first down running and with no open receiver in front of him he threw the ball away.

Quinn said he spoke to Daniels about the play.

"Even when you know there's a penalty, you still take your shot, man, to go throw it, complete it," Quinn said. "You don't know if it's gonna get picked up."

As it turned out the penalty wasn't an offsides call on the defense, which would have given Washington a first down. Rather it was an illegal shift on the Commanders.

"I didn't know. It could have been offside, it could have been on us," Daniels said if he anticipated an offsides call.

San Francisco declined the penalty because of the incompletion.

Daniels did complete 29-of-40 passes for 300 yards and two touchdowns on Monday night. He helped Washington rally from a 20-3 halftime deficit and drove the Commanders deep into 49ers territory late in the game with a chance to take the lead.

"Like most things with him, there's some plays that you said, that's an incredible throw," Quinn said. "And there's other ones I'd love him to stay through the [read]."

He said he knew it would be tough for Daniels to gain yards scrambling because of the 49ers' team speed and their zone coverage with eyes on the quarterback. Indeed he rushed only four times for 10 yards.

Daniels was playing his second game wearing a brace on his left elbow that he dislocated in Week 2. Quinn said as Daniels evolves in coordinator David Blough's offense he'd like him to scramble more to throw. But he also knows he can make plays multiple ways.

"He always can make some throws that just kinda leaves you thinking, 'Man, there it is. There's only a few guys that can make that throw or that play,'" Quinn said.

articles.headline: Barcelona, PSG thriller in Champions League proves these are the two best
articles.description: Both PSG and Barcelona got their first tastes of adversity this season in Tuesday's Champions League thriller, and it was a treat to watch.
articles.headlineJa: チャンピオンズリーグでのバルセロナ対PSGの熱戦、両者が最高峰の2チームであることを証明
articles.descriptionJa: 火曜日のチャンピオンズリーグでのスリリングな一戦で、PSGとバルセロナの両チームは今シーズン初めての苦境を味わったが、観る者を楽しませる素晴らしい試合となった。
articles.body:
Paris Saint-Germain produced a ruthless performance at Parc des Princes to end Barcelona's perfect start to the season, beating the visitors 4-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday and showing why PSG are still the best club side in the world.

PSG, aiming to win a third successive Champions League this season, saw Barca twice come back and cancel out leads from goals by Désiré Doué and Lucas Hernández with their equalisers from Xavi Espart and Lamine Yamal.

Barcelona went into the game having won all 11 games played so far in all competitions this season, but despite Yamal's stunning 79th minute equaliser, the LaLiga champions couldn't stop Luis Enrique's side in Paris.

It was vintage PSG as they did what they have done so often in the Champions League by finding another gear in the closing stages to blow away a formidable opponent. An 81st minute Vitinha strike restored PSG's lead for a third and final time, and Fabián Ruiz made the game safe with the fourth goal five minutes later.

This was a statement win by PSG, but with Barcelona keeping an eye toward Real Madrid next up in El Clasico on Sunday, Barca showed why they can be a genuine threat to the French club's hopes of a Champions League three-peat this season. -- Mark Ogden

• Live: Watch El Clasico, 3 p.m. ET Sunday on ESPN+

Barcelona and PSG live up to billing as world's best teams

PSG and Barcelona went into this game as the two best club teams in the world: PSG as back-to-back Champions League winners, and Barca as the unstoppable force that had made a perfect start to this season with 11 wins from 11 games.

Something had to give in Paris -- and ultimately it was Barcelona's winning streak. After a thrilling back and forth, PSG showed Hansi Flick's Barcelona what it takes to be the No. 1.

But don't let that take anything away from Barca. They played their part in an incredible game at Parc des Princes and made PSG look human -- for 80 minutes anyway.

On the flip side, PSG's level also made Barcelona look ordinary at times when they are anything but. But when two sides of such absolute quality go head-to-head, they live up to the hype by showing the very best of themselves.

PSG ran rampant against Manchester City in a 4-2 win at the Etihad last week, but they controlled that game and never looked in danger of losing. It was a different story against Barca, who made them work harder than at any time since last season's Champions League final against Arsenal. PSG had to step up and they did.

But so did Barcelona. Even in defeat, they showcased why they can win the Champions League this season. Lamine Yamal's stunning goal showed he can beat the best on his own and he will no doubt do that this season.

So, while Barca's winning run ends, they showed they are a worthy rival to PSG. But PSG are still the gold standard for everyone to aspire to. -- Ogden

articles.headline: Sources: Rams signing free agent kicker Brandon McManus
articles.description: The Rams, after releasing Harrison Mevis and an injury to Blake Grupe, are signing free agent kicker Brandon McManus, sources told NFL Network.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者発表：ラムズがフリーエージェントのキッカー、ブランドン・マクマナスと契約へ
articles.descriptionJa: NFL Networkが伝えた関係者の話によると、ラムズはハリソン・メビスの放出とブレイク・グルーペの負傷を受け、フリーエージェントのキッカーであるブランドン・マクマナスと契約する。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- The Rams are signing kicker Brandon McManus, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo on Tuesday.

The Rams worked out McManus and free agent kicker Matt Prater on Tuesday after kicker Blake Grupe tore his ACL in a Week 6 loss to the Arizona Cardinals.

Grupe was playing in his first game for the Rams after he was signed to replace Harrison Mevis, who missed a 50-yard field goal attempt and then had a 48-yarder blocked in overtime of the Rams' Week 5 loss.

McManus last kicked for the Green Bay Packers after signing with them in 2024. He was 44 of 51 for Green Bay over two seasons, with six misses coming during the 2025 season.

He spent his first nine seasons with the Denver Broncos and one with the Jacksonville Jaguars and was not on a roster to start the 2024 season while being investigated by the NFL for possible violations of the personal conduct policy. In September 2024, the NFL announced McManus was not in violation of the policy and he signed with the Packers three weeks later.

articles.headline: Kon Knueppel, Coby White out for Hornets' season opener
articles.description: The Hornets will be without guards Kon Knueppel and Coby White as well as veteran forward Grant Williams as they open their season Wednesday at Brooklyn.
articles.headlineJa: ホーネッツのシーズン開幕戦、コン・ニューペルとコービー・ホワイトが欠場
articles.descriptionJa: 水曜日にブルックリンでの開幕戦を迎えるホーネッツは、ガードのコン・ニューペルとコービー・ホワイト、そしてベテランフォワードのグラント・ウィリアムズが欠場する。
articles.body:
The Charlotte Hornets will be without guards Kon Knueppel and Coby White as well as veteran forward Grant Williams as they open their season Wednesday at the Brooklyn Nets.

Knueppel, who was the first rookie to lead the league with 273 made 3-pointers last season, injured his left hamstring during offseason on-court activity and missed the entire preseason.

White suffered a left calf strain Oct. 5 during training camp and missed the remainder of preseason.

Williams was ruled out for all four of Charlotte's preseason games because of a right hamstring injury.

The team said Tuesday that all three players have resumed individual on-court activity.

The Hornets are hoping to rely on Knueppel and White this season after trading LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves over the summer. Knueppel averaged 18.5 points, 5.3 rebounds and 42.5% 3-point shooting as a rookie.

The Hornets acquired White from the Chicago Bulls in February, and he went on to have a strong finish to the season with his new team. He was the hero in the team's play-in victory over the Miami Heat, scoring 19 points and hitting the turnaround 3 late in regulation to force overtime. He signed a three-year, $74 million contract with Charlotte over the summer.

Williams has averaged 7.2 points and 3.7 rebounds per game during his seven seasons.

articles.headline: NBA opening day: Live updates, highlights from tripleheader
articles.description: The 2026-27 NBA season is back with a bang. Follow along for all of the live updates and highlights from the tripleheader.
articles.headlineJa: NBA開幕日：3試合同時開催のライブ速報とハイライト
articles.descriptionJa: 2026-27 NBAシーズンが華々しく開幕。3試合同時開催のライブ速報とハイライトを随時お届けします。
articles.body:
The NBA is back with a bang.

The 2026-27 season tips off with a tripleheader, beginning with a rare daytime game between the Detroit Pistons and Boston Celtics. That sets up ring night at Madison Square Garden as the New York Knicks host the Philadelphia 76ers. The night concludes with a rematch of the 2026 Western Conference finals between the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder.

Each game bring its own headlines, starting off in Detroit. The Pistons are coming off a 60-win season, while the Celtics debut the duo of Jayson Tatum and Paul George.

The Knicks are raising a banner for the first time in 50 years. Who will look to spoil their night? None other than the new-look 76ers, with Jaylen Brown and LeBron James teaming up with Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe. 

Five months after defeating Oklahoma City in Game 7 to reach the Finals, San Antonio welcomes its Western Conference rivals in another battle. The Thunder and Spurs return most of their cores, setting up a matchup full of familiar matchups and tension.

We'll have all of the top moments and highlights from the NBA's tripleheader. Follow along below.

articles.headline: Champions League recap: PSG defeat Barça in classic, 40 goals across nine matches
articles.description: Paris Saint-Germain defeated Barcelona in a thrilling encounter on a Tuesday full of goals in the UEFA Champions League.
articles.headlineJa: チャンピオンズリーグまとめ：PSGが名勝負の末にバルサを撃破、9試合で計40ゴールが記録される
articles.descriptionJa: UEFAチャンピオンズリーグにおいて、ゴールが乱発する熱戦となった火曜日に、パリ・サンジェルマンがバルセロナを下す激闘を繰り広げた。
articles.body:
The Champions!

Another week, which means another round of European heavyweights facing off against each other.

The UEFA Champions League returned Tuesday for Matchday 3 of the league phase, with nine matches across the continent and plenty of mouthwatering clashes on the schedule.

Among the standout fixtures, defending champions Paris Saint-Germain welcomed Barcelona in a blockbuster showdown, and it lived up to the hype as the hosts won 4-2; Liverpool hosted Villarreal at Anfield, where the Reds were able to win 4-3, and Atlético Madrid traveled to Germany to face Stuttgart, where it ended in a 1-1 draw.

Elsewhere, Manchester City took on AEK Athens as the hosts won 5-1, while Napoli hosted Bodø/Glimt and ended up winning 4-3.

In our two early matches, we had Fenerbahçe and Slavia Prague facing off against each other as the match ended 2-2, and Sabah hosted Borussia Dortmund, where the German club got a 2-1 win away in Azerbaijan.

The other matches of the day included AS Roma beating Slovan Bratislava 4-0, and PSV Eindhoven were able to beat FC Porto 1-0.

Enjoy all that happened from Tuesday's matches across Europe.

articles.headline: Mac Allister, Ngumoha lead Liverpool rally to stay perfect in UCL
articles.description: Teenage winger Rio Ngumoha announced himself to the Champions League as Liverpool extended their 100% record the hard way as they came from two goals down to beat Villarreal 4-3.
articles.headlineJa: マック・アリスターとングモハがリヴァプールの猛追を牽引、UCLで全勝を維持
articles.descriptionJa: 10代のウィング、リオ・ングモハがチャンピオンズリーグでの存在感を示した。リヴァプールはビジャレアルに対し2点差を追いついて4-3で逆転勝利を収め、UCLでの全勝記録を維持した。
articles.body:
Teenage winger Rio Ngumoha announced himself to the Champions League as Liverpool extended their 100% record the hard way as they came from two goals down to beat Villarreal 4-3.

A night which began terribly with a Virgil van Dijk mistake ended with plenty of positives for the hosts as 18-year-old Ngumoha took the starring role as Alexis Mac Allister scored twice and Florian Wirtz grabbed his first since April.

Andoni Iraola's team are establishing themselves as Europe's great entertainers as after six goals at LASK last week another four left them behind only Paris St Germain in the table and as the competition's top scorers.

Having changed the game as a second-half substitute at Brentford on Saturday, Ngumoha returned to the starting line-up as one of six changes after another injury denied them Víctor Muñoz.

But in a chastening first half-hour the 18-year-old was not immune from the malaise which affected the team as, after Van Dijk headed into the path of Georges Mikautadze for the opener, he failed to track his runner allowing Sergi Cardona to double the lead.

After that, Ngumoha proceeded to make the Villarreal left back's life a misery with a captivating performance of pacy dribbling.

He crossed for Ronald Araújo to equalise on the stroke of halftime, the on-loan Barcelona defender disappearing into the front row of the Anfield Road stand where he was mobbed by fans, after Mac Allister's flicked header had reduced the deficit.

Ngumoha returned even more threatening after the break and from one of a number of attacking drives which tormented Cardona Mac Allister rammed home from close range.

Anfield hailed the youngster's mercurial talent and he departed to a 74th-minute standing ovation, with Duran Duran's "Rio" played at the final whistle.

articles.headline: Foden hat trick fuels emphatic Man City win as Haaland rested
articles.description: Phil Foden scored a hat trick as Manchester City got their Champions League campaign back on track with an emphatic 5-1 win over AEK Athens.
articles.headlineJa: フォーデンがハットトリック、ハーランド休息の中マン・シティが圧勝
articles.descriptionJa: フィル・フォーデンがハットトリックを記録。マンチェスター・シティはAEKアテネに5-1で快勝し、チャンピオンズリーグでの戦いを軌道に乗せ直した。
articles.body:
Phil Foden scored a hat trick as Manchester City got their Champions League campaign back on track with an emphatic 5-1 win over AEK Athens.

Elliot Anderson, with his first goal for the club, and Rayan Cherki were also on the scoresheet in a one-sided contest at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday.

The Greek champions rallied early in the second half to cut the deficit to 2-1 through Stavros Palios but it was a rare moment of quality from the visitors.

City were superior in all departments even with a much-changed side as Enzo Maresca gave opportunities to fringe players.

Top scorer Erling Haaland, rested after an injury scare, remained rooted to the bench throughout.

Youngster Floyd Samba took the Norwegian's place up front but the night was largely about Foden.

After two indifferent seasons and a frustrating start to the current one after his sending off in last month's Manchester derby, the midfielder has returned in style in the past few days.

articles.headline: NFL to increase security in Paris for Steelers-Saints game
articles.description: The NFL said security will be heightened for the game in Paris between the Steelers and Saints after civil unrest engulfed the French capital last weekend.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- The NFL said security will be heightened for the game in Paris between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints on Sunday after civil unrest engulfed the French capital last weekend.

Executive VP of club business, international and league events Peter O'Reilly said officials are collaborating with Parisian and national authorities overseas, along with the U.S. State Department. League officials, including senior VP of security Cathy Lanier, have been on the ground in France, according to O'Reilly.

"There's nothing more important from our standpoint than the teams' security, the fans' security -- everybody involved with this game," O'Reilly said at the league's annual fall owners meeting. "Obviously being very vigilant in everything we do, in all of our planning on an hour-by-hour basis, working closely with the two teams."

O'Reilly said there was never a point that the game was in danger of not being played at Stade de France, which is in the outskirts of Paris in Saint-Denis. He cited other sporting events ongoing in the city, including a Champions League soccer match between Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona on Tuesday night.

The NFL has in the past moved games to avoid getting in the way of local response to an unforeseen event, and officials believe that is not an issue for the league's debut in France.

"We feel confident that we would not have any impact on the broader resources needed," O'Reilly said. "That's always top of mind for us, and we feel confident that we wouldn't be depleting resources in a negative way around this game."

Rioters clashed with police, set cars on fire, stormed public buildings and engulfed a historic city hall in flames in France's worst civil unrest in years as violence and looting swept through major cities.

About 2,400 people were arrested over the weekend, and authorities said thousands of businesses were damaged or looted. The rioting overshadowed demonstrations against rising living costs and poor conditions in schools in which hundreds of thousands of people marched peacefully.

The Saints traveled directly to Paris after playing at the New York Giants and are practicing in the area this week. The Steelers are set to travel closer to kickoff.

With the collective bargaining agreement allowing for up to 10 international games, O'Reilly said that number is being considered for next season. There are a record nine on the schedule this year.

Where those games take place is still being discussed.

"We like continuity, but we are looking at new regions, and Asia would be one of them," O'Reilly said.

After so much talk leading up to and coming out of the game in Melbourne, Australia, about the Los Angeles Rams waiting until late to fly there -- and lost 27-7 to San Francisco -- the NFL does not appear close to dictating when teams must travel.

articles.headline: Wizards' AJ Dybantsa (ankle) to miss season opener
articles.description: AJ Dybantsa, the No. 1 pick in the NBA draft, will miss the Wizards' season opener Wednesday because of an ankle injury.
articles.body:
The Washington Wizards will have to wait a little longer before seeing the regular-season debut of their No. 1 pick.

AJ Dybantsa will miss the team's Wednesday night season opener against the Milwaukee Bucks with an ankle injury, coach Brian Keefe announced Tuesday.

Dybantsa will be day-to-day with the injury he suffered in Friday's preseason finale. Keefe termed the injury a mild ankle sprain Friday.

Dybantsa fell to the ground after landing awkwardly on his left ankle following a midrange jump shot before limping to the locker room. He had scored 12 points in 15 minutes before his exit in the second quarter.

The next chance for Dybantsa to make his debut would be Friday night at home against the Toronto Raptors before the team plays at Chicago on Saturday in the first of three straight road games.
